t: Berkeley-POLITICO poll: 51% of California voters oppose new data centers
b: A Sept. 8-14 survey of 2,418 registered voters found 51% opposed to new data centers statewide and 61% opposed in their own community. Only 3% named data centers and AI the top issue, and few want the state to hold more authority.
iw: Majority opposition, though low issue salience limits near-term political pressure.

t: Big Tech and PG&E ramp up Sacramento lobbying on data center bills
b: CalMatters reported heavy 2026 lobbying on data center bills: PG&E spent $2.86 million in one quarter, Amazon over $500,000 in six months across 33 bills, and the Data Center Coalition opposed nearly every regulatory bill.
iw: Industry is actively contesting regulation, with uncertain effect on outcomes.

t: PPIC survey: 73% of Californians oppose data centers in their communities
b: PPIC's July 2026 environment survey of 1,578 adults found 73% oppose building data centers in their communities, with majorities of both parties opposed, and 63% worried about environmental effects.
iw: Broad bipartisan local opposition raises political risk for new projects.

t: Advocacy poll: 70% oppose local data centers, but guardrails win majority support
b: A poll by FM3 for Net-Zero California and TURN, fielded May 17-24 among 850 likely voters, found 70% opposed to local data centers. Support reached 63% with protections against bill increases and environmental harm; 74% want standards in law.
iw: Opposition is strong, yet voters accept projects meeting cost and environmental conditions.

t: Over 300 Pittsburg residents urge council to block approved data center
b: More than 300 people attended a Pittsburg City Council meeting to oppose a data center on the former Delta View golf course, approved in 2024. Speakers asked for a ban or two-year pause, and a petition drew about 13,000 signatures in a week.
iw: Organized local opposition threatens an already-approved project.
